newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stars lobby PM on Aboriginal land rights.
newsitem.headline: Australian stars lobby PM on Aboriginal land rights.

text.p: More than 100 leading Australians, including some of the country's top movie and sports stars, on Thursday urged the government to stand firm against calls to abolish Aboriginal native title land rights.

The prominent figures, including Academy Award-winning actor Geoffrey Rush and Booker prize-winning author Peter Carey, wrote to Prime Minister John Howard asking him to protect Aborigines in a land rights row with farmers.
"We ask you to be courageous and not give in to the destructive forces of selfishness, prejudice or ignorance," their letter said.
"We believe that this path could lead to the most serious damage to the social fabric of Australian society and to our standing in the international community. Do not diminish our nation."
Howard is under pressure from farm groups and the National Party, the junior partner in his Liberal-National coalition, to abolish Aboriginal rights to government land leased to farmers.
He has proposed a compromise confirming farmers' rights, but guaranteeing Aborigines limited access for traditional purposes.
Farmers and miners say the row, sparked by a December court decision that Aborigines still had rights to land under pastoral leases, has damaged their multi-billion industries.
